changes.after: PHP can insert a stored value into text inside double quotes.

before: Double-quoted strings can insert variable values and interpret escapes such as \n. Single-quoted strings do not interpolate variables; most backslashes remain literal.
The dot operator joins two strings. It is different from numeric addition with +.
"Hello {$name}" clearly marks the variable name inside double quotes. It does not change the value stored in that variable.
Expected output or behavior: Hello Mira. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Compare interpolation with "Hello " . $name and explain which parts are literal text. You may trace it without a PHP interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
